body:
this method is a member function while `_get_dropped_resource_str_line` is a static function not related to `ScriptTextEditor`

come to think of it is already shady `_get_dropped_resource_str_line` exists here, because this class is not GdScript specific, and these functions are 🤔

naming for these functions and conditions feels wrong, difference is not about what is being dropped (a string or a ref) difference is about what kind of line is being created (variable or export)

I would suggest some renamings:
`str_drop_modifier_pressed` to `member_drop_modifier_pressed `
`ref_drop_modifier_pressed` to`export_drop_modifier_pressed`
`_get_dropped_resource_str_line` to `_get_dropped_resource_as member`
`_get_dropped_resource_ref_line` to `_get_dropped_resource_as_exported_member`
I agree, ill change those.

> come to think of it is already shady _get_dropped_resource_str_line exists here, because this class is not GdScript specific, and these functions are 🤔

Yeah I agree, that what i was confused about too.. But i was trying to follow the existing structure.

> this method is a member function while _get_dropped_resource_str_line is a static function not related to ScriptTextEditor

The problem I had is that I couldn't find a nice way to do this inside `drop_data_fw` without it feeling dirty, since you would have to assign the exported variables AFTER they have been created, maybe even would have to reload the script? So instead I did it at a later time, inside `_validate_script()`, which means i have to keep some list of the nodes/files that were dragged in as a member of the class, which means the method cannot be static..

Ill try to see what happens if i do this in the same  `drop_data_fw` after inserting the new text(maybe the script is reloaded there, need to debug). That way i can keep it confined to that method only.
renamed as your request
i changed the implementation to be cleaner, so its more self contained inside `drop_data_fw` instead of having class level members.

instead of connecting and disconnecting the signal you could use the flag CONNECT_ONESHOT

Is there any reason why you cannot just execute `_assign_dragged_export_variables` at the end of `drop_data_fw` ? i dont imagine `drop_data_fw` being called more than once in the same frame, as far as i can see it process all drops toguether instead of it being called several times.
Even if that was the case calling `_assign_dragged_export_variables` once per `drop_data_fw` doesn't look too bad

Do you need to wait until property_list_changed is called in the script? could a call deferred do the trick?

> Do you need to wait until property_list_changed is called in the script? could a call deferred do the trick?

I tried using `call_deffered`, it didn't seem to update the script variables in time before trying to assign them. I assume `property_list_changed` signal can work too, but `edited_script_changed` seems to work fine currently (unless you have a specific reason you prefer `property_list_changed`). Ill try checking.

**Edit:** connecting to `property_list_changed` does not seem to work for some reason. 

> instead of connecting and disconnecting the signal you could use the flag CONNECT_ONESHOT

Oh cool! I'll do that.

i was not suggesting to use `property_list_changed`, i was jsut asking if that was the reason :)

`property_list_changed` is not emitted when the script is modified, is an internal process ofan object that happens without changing the script (in example because a property "enable_feature" changes from false to true, and more properties related to the feature are added to the inspector)
I believe you could do `if (!global_resource_script_name.is_empty())`
`if (ResourceLoader::exists(path) && ( member_drop_modifier_pressed || export_drop_modifier_pressed))`
I feel the comment is useful, no need for deletion

The signal is being connected every time there is a dragged export. It'd be better to assign it in `ScriptTextEditor::_enable_code_editor`. Still weird it does not update it when you emit the signal after the call though.
i believe the reason to connect it here is to `bind` additional arguments
As a workaround, the dictionary could be defined in the header file, so it's global and it doesn't try to connect multiple times, when once is already fine.
yes, that was the initial implementation

> The signal is being connected every time there is a dragged export. It'd be better to assign it in `ScriptTextEditor::_enable_code_editor`.

I don't really agree, this would call the `_assign_dragged_export_variables` function every time the signal `edited_script_changed` is being emitted, when very often it won't be necessary. I figure its best to have a small overhead for every time you drag and drop to create an export variable, rather than every single time you change _anything_ in the current edited script. 

> Still weird it does not update it when you emit the signal after the call though.

Don't know what you mean by that.

> As a workaround, the dictionary could be defined in the header file, so it's global and it doesn't try to connect multiple times, when once is already fine.

Yes, as @MarianoGnu said that was the original implementation, but it felt a bit weird to have it in a global level imo.

i believe in general is cheaper an early return in `_assign_dragged_export_variables` when `dragged_export_refs.is_empty()` than the time and memory it takes to allicate a new `callable_mp(this, &ScriptTextEditor::_assign_dragged_export_variables).bind(dragged_export_refs)` every time you drag and drop stuff. **But:**
A. we havent benchmarked it
B. is super premature optimization
I dont care using one implementation or the other
